bullets.title: NVDA invests $5B in Ilya Sutskever's Safe Superintelligence; gains Vera chip access
bullets.body: NVIDIA committed $5 billion to Ilya Sutskever's Safe Superintelligence (SSI) startup and announced a long-term partnership giving SSI access to next-generation Vera chips. The deal signals continued NVDA investment in frontier AI R&D beyond its hardware supply chain.

bullets.title: NVDA & MSFT launch open AI security alliance — excluding OpenAI, Google, Anthropic
bullets.body: Satya Nadella and Jensen Huang announced a joint alliance to advance AI security within the frontier AI ecosystem. Notably, OpenAI, Google, and Anthropic were excluded from the partnership.

bullets.title: Apple reclaims world's largest company title from NVIDIA; AAPL +16% MTD vs NVDA negative
bullets.body: Apple's market cap of ~$4.95T edged past NVIDIA's ~$4.81–4.9T, reclaiming the top spot. AAPL has rallied ~16% month-to-date while NVDA has turned negative for the month, previously the last semiconductor holdout before also reversing.

bullets.title: Semis down ~4% while software rallies 3% — sharp sector rotation underway
bullets.body: The semiconductor index fell nearly 4% on the day while the software index (IGV) rallied ~3%, reflecting a significant sector unwind. QQQ reversed a 1%+ opening gain within 30 minutes, with NVDA showing the most bearish options flow and MU falling 6.1% below $1T market cap.

bullets.title: China begins mass production of domestic DUV lithography tools; ASML halted, -7-8%
bullets.body: The Information reported China has started mass-producing homegrown DUV chipmaking equipment, initially targeting 5 units this year scaling to 20 by 2027. ASML shares were suspended after falling 6-8% on the news, while some analysts argue the panic is overblown and suggest buying the dip in chip stocks.

bullets.title: CXMT debuts +466% to $484B market cap — Goldman warns of 'new problem' for memory industry
bullets.body: Chinese DRAM maker CXMT surged 466% on its first trading day to a ~$484–488B market cap, making it mainland China's largest listed company and bigger than Intel. Goldman Sachs flagged the IPO as a 'new problem' for the memory industry, while CXMT is also reportedly set to receive domestically developed DUV machines in August.

bullets.title: MSFT Copilot sales beat expectations in FY26Q4; Azure capacity/pricing trends positive
bullets.body: A preview note on MSFT's 2Q26 results expects Copilot sales to have beaten prior expectations with improving user experience. Azure capacity and pricing trends are also seen as improving despite intense AI competition. Separately, market commentary flagged that Microsoft capex-cut fears may be misplaced.

bullets.title: Hyperscaler capex projected at $1.4T by 2028; Moody's warns on credit quality of AMZN, META, GOOGL
bullets.body: Top hyperscalers are forecast to spend $426B in 2025, $600B+ in 2026, $1T+ in 2027, and $1.4T in 2028 on AI data centers. Moody's flagged 'unprecedented' AI spending as a threat to the credit quality of Amazon, Meta, and Alphabet, while Mark Cuban quipped excess data centers could become 'pickleball courts.'

bullets.title: AMZN signs $4B compute deal with Pinterest on AWS Trainium; Kuiper proposes 5,105-satellite constellation
bullets.body: Amazon reportedly signed a $4B long-term compute deal with Pinterest using AWS Trainium chips — one fintwit account frames this as evidence the real AI bottleneck is compute providers, not just semis. Separately, Amazon's Project Kuiper proposed a 5,105-satellite LEO constellation for direct mobile device connectivity launching in 2028.

bullets.title: YouTube Premium to bundle Peacock starting early 2025 — GOOGL/CMCSA deal confirmed
bullets.body: YouTube TV and Peacock announced a new content distribution deal providing YouTube Premium subscribers in the U.S. access to all Peacock content including live sports. The deal expands Google's content value proposition while providing CMCSA/Peacock with a new distribution channel.

bullets.title: GOOGL crosses back above $4T market cap; GCP showing ROI inflection per analyst
bullets.body: Google climbed back above a $4 trillion market cap during the session. One analyst note flagged GOOGL GCP as showing an ROI inflection as a bullish catalyst alongside NOW's 2Q26 pull-forward demand.

bullets.title: NAND price weakness flagged as 'canary in AI stock coalmine'; semi cycle concerns
bullets.body: One fintwit account highlighted NAND price declines as a warning signal for the broader AI stock momentum trade, noting prices can precede wider semiconductor softness. A separate contrarian noted they had warned against semis at the peak despite crowd pushback, calling out MU, AMD, INTC, NVDA.

bullets.title: Intel 18A-P and 14A secure Cadence full EDA toolchain in foundry push vs. TSMC
bullets.body: Intel's advanced process nodes 18A-P and 14A gained access to Cadence's complete EDA toolchain, a move seen as tightening Intel's foundry ecosystem competitiveness against TSMC. Cadence's full support signals confidence in Intel's advanced manufacturing capability.

bullets.title: TSLA: Deutsche Bank cuts PT to $420 (from $465), maintains Buy; stock at multi-year lows
bullets.body: Deutsche Bank's Edison Yu cut the Tesla price target to $420 from $465 while maintaining a Buy rating. TSLA is trading at the same level as one year ago and as October 2021, effectively showing no net price progress. Separately, commentary suggests Elon's September 2025 stock purchase was exclusively to boost shareholder morale for comp package approval and will not be repeated.

bullets.title: Semiconductor valuation warning: chipmaker multiples now exceed dot-com bubble peak
bullets.body: Multiple fintwit accounts noted that US chipmaker valuations are now higher than at the peak of the dot-com bubble, flagging that AI's revolutionary potential doesn't negate the importance of entry price for investment returns.

bullets.title: Fed: 36% probability of hike at Wednesday's FOMC; futures pricing 1.75 hikes by year-end
bullets.body: Fed funds futures show an unusual 36% probability of a rate hike at Wednesday's FOMC meeting — one of only ~4 meetings since 2009 with this level of pre-meeting uncertainty. Futures are pricing 1.75 total hikes by year-end, and the 2-year yield spread vs. the effective rate is at levels historically seen before 500+ bps of hikes. Goldman expects the Fed to hold while markets price more aggressive action.

bullets.title: Goldman quant: 'July Has Been A Long Year' — markets finally pricing structural concerns
bullets.body: Goldman's top quant trader warned that markets are 'no longer' ignoring underlying structural conditions, calling July a turning point in market psychology. Goldman separately noted rising oil volatility is shifting investor focus from earnings to macro risks including inflation and higher rates.

bullets.title: Global bond yields hit 2008 highs; 30-yr Treasury at 5.17%, highest weekly close since July 2007
bullets.body: Global bond yields rose to their highest levels since 2008, with the 30-year US Treasury closing last week at 5.17% — its highest weekly close since July 2007. One account characterized the move as reflecting market skepticism about official inflation narratives.

bullets.title: Tech sector ($XLK) on pace for worst month since September 2022
bullets.body: The technology sector ETF (XLK) is tracking its worst monthly performance since September 2022. One portfolio tracker noted QQQ is down -8.01% and XLK down -8.83%, with only select Mag 7 names outperforming.

bullets.title: HOOD: Robinhood cut 290 staff (10%) amid broader crypto sector contraction
bullets.body: Robinhood announced 290 layoffs representing ~10% of its workforce as part of a broader crypto sector contraction that also saw Coinbase cut 500 employees (14%). Multiple crypto platforms were simultaneously filing for bankruptcy or winding down, per a fintwit roundup.
